cases.question: Can compact card search paginate and bound the result set before hydration?
criteria: card response shape stays compact and uses dedupe_key
limit is honored before hydration, keeping payload size bounded
the result surface does not widen to full hydrated results
failureCriteria: hydrating the full candidate set before limiting
returning the wrong payload shape or omitting dedupe keys
client-side reranking after the backend has already paginated
cases.validator: Existing assertions in scripts/test-recipe-backend.php fail if the compact card result shape, limit, or size bound changes.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger can describe search code, but usually misses the ordering of pagination, hydration, and bounded output that the frozen test enforces.

cases.question: Does minimum coverage filter the candidate set before page slicing?
criteria: every returned item satisfies the coverage threshold
pagination happens after thresholding, not before
the returned page is not padded with below-threshold items
failureCriteria: filtering after pagination and accidentally leaking low-coverage rows
using reranked client state instead of the backend filter
returning a page that is underfilled because thresholding happened too late
cases.validator: The backend test asserts the coverage condition directly and will fail if any returned item falls below 1.0 coverage.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger often treats coverage as a soft preference; the frozen case requires it to be a hard pre-pagination gate.

cases.question: Do cursors stay pinned to their score/catalog snapshot during imports, and invalidate when ordering changes?
criteria: page 2 keeps the same snapshot_id and total as page 1
late imports do not leak into an already-issued cursor
ordering-changing updates invalidate the old cursor
failureCriteria: reading current state instead of the pinned snapshot
allowing a stale cursor to continue after an ordering change
recomputing totals or page content from the latest catalog state
cases.validator: The test asserts snapshot_id equality, late-import exclusion, and cursor rejection after an order-changing update.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger may understand pagination in the abstract but miss the snapshot pinning and invalidation boundary that protects cursor correctness.

cases.question: Does text search apply pantry ranking before slicing each page in both stocked and expiring modes?
criteria: the first ranked result is the cookable recipe in both modes
ranking is evaluated before the limit is applied
the backend order, not a frontend rerank, determines the page
failureCriteria: ranking after pagination
ignoring the mode-specific ranking path
changing the first item because of client-side reranking
cases.validator: The test compares the first result id in both stocked and expiring modes against the expected cookable recipe.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger tends to collapse search and ranking into one generic score; this case checks the backend mode split and the ordering boundary explicitly.

cases.question: Does stocked ranking ignore expiry while expiring ranking uses it and still gates cookability?
criteria: stocked scores are insensitive to expiry changes
expiring scores change when expiry becomes relevant
missing required ingredients still gate cookability
failureCriteria: leaking expiry into stocked ranking
letting expiry rescue an un-cookable recipe
ignoring the hard missing-ingredient gate
cases.validator: The test asserts equal stocked scores across far-apart expiries and a lower expiring score for the same recipe, plus a cookability check.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger may treat all ranking modes the same; the frozen case proves the mode-specific score model matters.

cases.question: Do recommendations preserve unique ordered card summaries at both 30 and 70 item limits?
criteria: 30-item recommendations contain 30 unique dedupe keys
70-item recommendations also contain 70 unique dedupe keys
the response stays non-degraded
failureCriteria: front-end reranking or post-hoc dedupe
duplicate dedupe keys in the ordered summary list
dropping the higher requested limit or degrading the response
cases.validator: The test checks exact counts, dedupe-key uniqueness, and the degraded flag for both limits.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger can generate plausible ranking language, but this case measures the exact uniqueness and order contract at two different page sizes.

cases.question: Does the frozen ontology gold still expand to the required food-case and false-equivalence counts?
criteria: generated food cases meet the minimum corpus size
false-equivalence pairs meet the minimum threshold
legitimate food cases reach exact identity and not review/failure
failureCriteria: contaminating the frozen gold set
shrinking the corpus or the false-equivalence coverage
treating the gold fixture as a generated snapshot instead of frozen evaluation data
cases.validator: The coverage script deterministically counts generated cases, false pairs, and per-case exact-identity admissions.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger can summarize ontology rules, but this case requires the exact frozen corpus expansion and threshold logic from the repository.

cases.question: Do representative cases preserve locale isolation and refuse taxonomy-trap equivalence?
criteria: representative cases admit exact identity for the intended language
taxonomy-trap sea lavender stays distinct from lavender
English locale variants converge while de and und stay isolated
failureCriteria: using taxonomy ancestry as identity
collapsing multilingual cases into one entity
letting undetermined locale bleed into language-specific resolution
cases.validator: The coverage script asserts representative admissions, false-pair rejection, and locale-specific resolution behavior.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger is likely to overgeneralize synonym or locale logic; this case checks the precise trap and isolation boundaries.

cases.question: Do invalid labels and prepared products fail closed without retry churn?
criteria: prepared products are rejected with the prepared_food reason
empty and punctuation-only labels resolve unresolved and null
permanently unsupported labels do not churn into needs_review or retry
failureCriteria: promoting malformed labels into identity admissions
turning prepared products into reviewable candidates
spinning retry loops for permanently unsupported inputs
cases.validator: The coverage script asserts prepared-product rejection, unresolved empty-label behavior, and bounded retry counters for unsupported labels.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger often misses the fail-closed terminal state and retries; the frozen case checks both the rejection reason and the absence of churn.

cases.question: Does exact-self admission stay off when disabled and publish immediately when enabled without creating needs_review rows?
criteria: exact-self admission is on by default but can be forced off in test mode
disabled baseline saves do not admit identity
enabled saves admit exact_self_identity and do not create needs_review rows
failureCriteria: publishing identity while the toggle is disabled
creating review churn for ordinary exact-self saves
failing to keep the admitted entity_id negative and exact-self sourced
cases.validator: The exact-identity product-save script asserts toggle behavior, accepted source, negative runtime entity ids, and zero needs_review rows.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger can narrate product-save flow, but this case requires the exact toggle semantics and the absence of review churn.

cases.question: Can background exact-self admission succeed even when canonical/provider queue work is absent?
criteria: the background job finishes and the annex status is accepted
the admission source remains exact_self_identity
canonical queue deletion does not block background admission
failureCriteria: coupling exact-self admission to canonical or provider work
leaving the background job unfinished
changing the admission source away from exact_self_identity
cases.validator: The script deletes queue work, processes the queue batch, and then asserts the background admission and annex status.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger may assume the admission pipeline depends on unrelated queue stages; this case proves the independence boundary.

cases.question: Does replaying exact identity refresh preserve the entity binding and snapshot prefix?
criteria: replaying an admitted product returns the same entity_id
the identity extension snapshot does not change across replay
a later snapshot advances exactly one revision and the old context cannot see the new entity
failureCriteria: appending extension revisions on an idempotent replay
allowing the old pinned context to see late-added entities
changing the admitted entity binding during replay
cases.validator: The coverage script snapshots before and after replay and asserts equality, then checks the late snapshot revision and context visibility.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger often misses pinned-prefix semantics; this case checks that replay is idempotent and that later context remains isolated.

cases.question: Which provider titles auto-accept, and which ones must fail closed or quarantine?
criteria: exact consistent provider titles auto-accept
generic, missing, and oversize-normalized titles stay unresolved or D8
provider text is treated as factual metadata only, not semantic gold
failureCriteria: treating provider text as ontology creation
auto-accepting generic any-type titles
accepting overlong normalized labels instead of quarantining them
cases.validator: The provider test counts accepted, unresolved, and D8 terminal dispositions directly from the database.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger often over-trusts provider text; this case checks the allowlist and the quarantine boundary explicitly.

cases.question: Do local/provider hard conflicts and base conflicts remain quarantined instead of becoming accepted mappings?
criteria: fresh/dried facet conflict maps to provider_local_conflict
provider/base conflicts are separated from hard facet conflicts
generic or conflicting titles never auto-accept
failureCriteria: collapsing base and hard conflicts into one bucket
leaving provider-local conflicts in accepted state
letting generic titles silently resolve to accepted mappings
cases.validator: The provider audit and count assertions verify consistency buckets, local-provider conflict counts, and quarantine outcomes.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger tends to resolve all provider signals the same way; this case checks the conflict taxonomy and the quarantine output.

cases.question: Do default-title edits invalidate the owner fingerprint without dirtying scores, and does restoring the source row make the fingerprint valid again?
criteria: default-title changes invalidate the immutable owner fingerprint
the score state does not dirty or rebuild unnecessarily
restoring the source row restores fingerprint validity and projection acceptance
failureCriteria: silently reusing a stale fingerprint after source edits
dirtying or rebuilding scores for metadata-only title changes
failing to recover validity after the source row is restored
cases.validator: The test captures the stored fingerprint, mutates the source row, expects a stale projection failure, then restores the source row and re-checks fingerprint validity.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger may miss the provenance immutability contract; this case requires exact fingerprint invalidation and recovery behavior.

cases.question: Does the online backup path copy from a read-only source, verify quick_check, and publish atomically?
criteria: the source backup is opened read-only
quick_check must pass before publication
publish happens via temp file rename, not overwrite
failureCriteria: opening the source database writable
skipping the integrity check before publishing
publishing the backup without an atomic rename
cases.validator: The backup function and its test both assert read-only source access, quick_check success, and final rename publication.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger might describe backup in general terms but miss the copied-database atomicity and integrity gate that the repository enforces.

cases.question: Do current-schema reconnects remain read-only while still registering the ontology guard functions?
criteria: query_only opens execute no writes on a current schema
guard functions are still registered on reconnect
SQLite lock detection and dangling transaction recovery remain intact
failureCriteria: writing during a read-only reconnect
skipping guard registration on an already-migrated database
misclassifying lock errors or leaking a transaction
cases.validator: The runtime test checks total_changes before and after query_only, guard return values, lock recognition, and rollback recovery.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger can implement a reconnection path, but this case checks the copy-safe no-write behavior and guard registration that make it safe.

cases.question: Do partial databases get repaired and older markers upgrade forward without being downgraded?
criteria: a previous schema marker upgrades by adding the missing reconciliation columns
a partial database recreates missing core tables
a newer-than-build schema fails closed without lowering the marker
failureCriteria: downgrading a newer schema marker
leaving partial databases with missing core tables
failing to add reconciliation evidence columns during upgrade
cases.validator: The runtime test asserts exact schema versions, table presence, and the added reconciliation columns after migration.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger might repair one path but not preserve forward-only schema safety; this case requires both repair and fail-closed behavior.

cases.question: Does the ontology controller scaffold refuse mutating commands unless write access and copied-database gates are present?
criteria: mutating controller commands require --write
generation work is copied-database only
the active database remains intake-only
failureCriteria: allowing a mutating path without write access
running generation work on the active database
omitting the copied-database safety gate from the scaffold
cases.validator: The CLI usage text and the controller test both assert the write and copied-database gating rules.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger may scaffold commands quickly but miss the safety gates that keep the controller from touching the live database.

cases.question: Does the proposal scaffold remain staging-only, network-gated, and free of automatic activation?
criteria: proposal output remains staging-only
work requires --allow-network and uses the configured proposal model without fallback
nothing in the scaffold auto-activates ontology changes
failureCriteria: adding a hidden activation path to the scaffold
introducing fallback model behavior
allowing runtime model calls without the explicit network gate
cases.validator: The script usage text and status output are static and directly expose the staging-only contract.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger might create a working skeleton but not preserve the no-activation and no-fallback boundaries that define the scaffold.

cases.question: Does the controller scaffold retry transient BEGIN IMMEDIATE contention and keep the transaction closed?
criteria: BEGIN IMMEDIATE contention is retried and then succeeds
the returned claim token matches the row token
no transaction remains open after the claim completes
failureCriteria: single-shot lock failure without retry
leaking an open transaction after claim
returning a token that does not match the persisted claim row
cases.validator: The test counts immediate-begin attempts, compares token equality, and checks that the database is not left in a transaction.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger may wire the command shape but miss the retry-safe claim protocol that the scaffold must preserve.

cases.question: Does repeating the migration leave job request order and cursor rollback unchanged?
criteria: request_generation and request_epoch remain stable across repeated migration
cursor marker rollback and reinsertion happen together
repeating migration does not reorder the job stream
failureCriteria: changing request order during a mechanical transform
bumping cursor state even though the migration rolled back
creating a partially applied migration marker
cases.validator: The backend test asserts unchanged request order and exact cursor rollback semantics after a synthetic migration fault.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger may rewrite code mechanically but miss the order-preserving and rollback-preserving invariants that the transform must keep.

cases.question: Do read-only reconnects stay no-op, and do no-op saves preserve ranking/source row identity?
criteria: current-schema reconnects cause no writes
guard functions still resolve on reopen
a no-op repository save preserves ranking and source row ids plus ontology identity
failureCriteria: writing during a reconnect that should be read-only
changing row ids during a no-op save
dropping ontology identity or corpus hash on a no-op rewrite
cases.validator: The runtime test checks total_changes under query_only, and the backend test asserts exact id preservation across no-op saves.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger can apply a transform that appears harmless but still alters IDs or writes during reconnect; this case catches both.

cases.question: After a mechanical source-row edit, does restoring the row restore fingerprint validity?
criteria: the fingerprint audit fails while the source row is stale
restoring the source row makes the fingerprint audit valid again
the restore does not require a semantic re-adjudication
failureCriteria: treating the stale row as still valid after a transform
requiring a fresh semantic adjudication for a pure restore
leaving the audit invalid after the exact source row is restored
cases.validator: The provider test captures the fingerprint before and after the restore and checks the audit validity and projection failure state directly.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger may perform the mechanical edit but miss the exact provenance recovery boundary that makes the transform safe.

cases.question: When source rows mutate after the reserved snapshot, does final publication fail closed and clean partial output?
criteria: the build throws on stale source mapping fingerprints or input changes
the failed requirement revision is marked failed
no partial requirement rows remain
failureCriteria: publishing stale data after the snapshot changed
leaving partial requirement output behind
masking the fingerprint drift instead of surfacing it
cases.validator: The test injects a source mutation after snapshot reservation and asserts failure status plus zero partial output rows.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger may reproduce the symptom but miss the root cause and cleanup contract that the test is isolating.

cases.question: Can a mutation before publication reservation ever emit a stale ready projection?
criteria: the race is rejected with an input-changed or stale-fingerprint error
the failed revision is not published as ready
the repository leaves no stale ready projection behind
failureCriteria: publishing a ready projection after the reservation race
accepting the stale data as valid
leaving an empty ready snapshot in place of a failed build
cases.validator: The test injects a publication-race mutation and checks the resulting failure message and the failed revision row counts.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger may not model the reservation race; this case proves the publication boundary is enforced and observable.

cases.question: Does a stale fingerprint audit block projection until the exact source row is restored?
criteria: the audit is invalid while the source row drift exists
projection throws a stale-fingerprint error
restoring the source row makes the audit valid again
failureCriteria: silently accepting stale source rows
building a requirement projection despite the audit failure
failing to recover when the exact original row is restored
cases.validator: The test checks the audit flag, catches the stale-fingerprint exception, and then restores the source row to revalidate.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger may suggest a fix, but the frozen case requires an exact repro of the stale audit and the recovery path.

cases.question: Do validation errors classify into the correct activation outcomes, and does canonical source transition only pass on a sealed current corpus?
criteria: live drift maps to live_inputs_changed
score-date drift maps to rebase_required
the canonical source transition only passes for the exact sealed corpus hash
failureCriteria: treating derivative errors as primary drift
accepting an invalid canonical source transition
collapsing all validation failures into the same outcome kind
cases.validator: The runtime test feeds synthetic validation errors and compares the returned drift codes and outcome kind exactly.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger may flatten the validation taxonomy; this case checks the exact drift-code split and the sealed-base transition rule.

cases.question: Do live reservations and file locks surface explicit phases instead of blocking or swallowing contention?
criteria: non-blocking file lock contention throws the explicit locked phase
an available reservation runs exactly one named phase
optional CDC pruning fails open and does not block the activation cycle
failureCriteria: blocking instead of returning an explicit retryable phase
running multiple phases for one reservation
making optional pruning block the activation path
cases.validator: The runtime test checks the lock exception phase, the phase list, and the CDC pruning result exactly.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger may implement a reservation callback but not the phase semantics and fail-open pruning boundary that activation requires.

cases.question: Do canonical query hashes preserve exact row materialization and key order under the bounded activation runtime?
criteria: streaming hashes match legacy stable JSON exactly
row-hash and map-hash outputs remain canonical and ordered
the activation database uses FILE temp storage and the configured busy timeout
failureCriteria: materializing the whole query in memory instead of streaming
changing JSON key order or row order in the hash
using the wrong temp store or busy timeout budget
cases.validator: The runtime test compares legacy and streaming hashes with hash_equals and checks the PRAGMA values directly.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger may produce a hash that looks right but does not preserve canonical streaming materialization or the temp-store budget.

cases.question: Is a dirty worktree rejected before release images are built?
criteria: dirty worktree exits with a non-zero status
the script refuses to continue before image tagging
the release target remains the operator fork only
failureCriteria: building or tagging from a dirty tree
ignoring the release-target restriction
continuing past the worktree check after a failure
cases.validator: The shell script exits 2 with a clear message when git status is not clean.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger may automate the build but miss the release gate that prevents unsafe publishing from a dirty checkout.

cases.question: Does the release script refuse to tag images when the manifest version is invalid?
criteria: the version is extracted from manifest.json
the version must be numeric/dot-only
invalid version text is rejected before the docker build stage
failureCriteria: tagging with an empty or malformed version
building images before validating the manifest version
accepting non-numeric version text
cases.validator: The shell script exits before building if the manifest version does not match the numeric pattern.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger may hard-code a tag or parse loosely; this case requires the manifest-driven numeric gate.

cases.question: Are both the app image and bridge image built from the exact HEAD revision and verified by OCI label?
criteria: both the app and bridge images are built with the exact revision as VCS_REF
the app tag and bridge tag are both emitted
each image label matches the resolved commit hash exactly
failureCriteria: building only one image
skipping the OCI revision-label verification
tagging images with a revision that differs from HEAD
cases.validator: The script inspects each built image and exits if the org.opencontainers.image.revision label does not equal the resolved git revision.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper challenger may build images successfully but miss the explicit revision-label check that makes the release reproducible.
